drafts.text:
A study @alexgroberman shared checked 6,682 local businesses. 85.6% were never named by ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, or Perplexity.

Good reviews alone didn't fix it. Businesses with a website got named 17.5% of the time. Without one, 4.4%.

Give every service its own page.
drafts.pattern: You can have X and still be invisible, plus study numbers (alexgroberman 4.1K, fresh, on-brand)
keywords: local businesses invisible in AI assistants despite reviews
drafts.video_tip: Video tip (@BourgAnthony, about 20 sec, vertical screen recording): ask ChatGPT and Gemini the same question, 'best [trade] in [your city]', side by side, and show which businesses each one names. Caption: 'Same question, two different answers.' Show only what's on screen; no claims about why a business was or wasn't named.
drafts.best_time_ct: Weekday late morning CT; the standing 8:54 AM slot works for one a day.

drafts.text:
AI can spit out a contractor website in an afternoon now. @DannPetty nailed it: AI is great at patterns, but good design is still what separates it.

For a trade business, good design is plain stuff. Number up top. Real job photos. One page per service.
drafts.video_tip: Video tip (@BourgAnthony, about 20 sec, vertical screen recording): ask ChatGPT and Gemini the same question, 'best [trade] in [your city]', side by side, and show which businesses each one names. Caption: 'Same question, two different answers.' Show only what's on screen; no claims about why a business was or wasn't named.
drafts.best_time_ct: Weekday late morning CT; the standing 8:54 AM slot works for one a day.

drafts.type: don't opt out of AI search
drafts.text:
@CyrusShepard looked at sites that opted out of Google's AI features. AI impressions went to zero, and regular organic clicks dropped too.

If you run a local business, don't hide from it. Make your pages worth citing: what you do, where you work, and proof you're licensed.

drafts.text:
@mhp_guy just posted the playbook for cold pitching websites to roofers and HVAC shops. If you own one, expect calls.

Before you say yes to anybody, me included, ask:

Whose name is the domain under?
Can I see live sites you built for trades?
Who fixes it when it breaks?
